name: GPU-based Voxelization (CUDA)

# GPU-based Voxelization (CUDA)
## Overview
GPU-based Voxelization accelerates the conversion of polygon meshes or geometric primitives into discrete volumetric representations by leveraging the massive parallelism of CUDA-capable GPUs [G]. It solves the performance bottleneck of CPU-based [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md), enabling [real-time voxelization](#2406-gpu-rasterization-based-octree-building.md) of high-polygon models [G]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by its direct use of CUDA kernels for parallel triangle processing and atomic memory updates, contrasting with CPU parallelization [Parallel CPU Voxelization](7135-parallel-cpu-voxelization.md) or specialized structures like linked lists [Per-Pixel Linked List Voxelization](1187-per-pixel-linked-list-voxelization.md) [G].
## Shared principles
See [GPU and Parallel Acceleration Voxelization](6878-gpu-and-parallel-acceleration-voxelization.md) for the family's shared principles.
## Subtopics

### [Vessel Voxelizer](2321-vessel-voxelizer.md)
Converts vascular line segments into fuzzy voxel volumes using [supersampling](#3493-supersampling.md) to estimate volume fractions [G]. It distinguishes itself from standard [binary voxelization](#2402-sdf-based-binary-voxelization.md) by estimating continuous volume intersections, making it suitable for rendering translucent vascular networks [G]. Choose it when rendering semi-transparent vascular structures requires accurate volume fraction estimation rather than binary occupancy [G].

### [Flexible Dual Grid Mesh Voxelization](2640-flexible-dual-grid-mesh-voxelization.md)
Determines active sparse voxels and solves an enhanced Quadratic Error Function (QEF) for dual vertex positions [G]. It serves as the foundational occupancy and geometry reconstruction stage for [O-Voxel](#3835-o-voxel.md), differing from siblings by strictly providing raw voxel indices and dual vertices without higher-level serialization [G]. Choose it when a sparse dual-grid representation is needed for geometry reconstruction or as a preprocessing step for O-Voxel [G].

### [CUDA Voxelizer GPU Voxelization](6757-cuda-voxelizer-gpu-voxelization.md)
An optimized implementation of Schwarz and Seidel's algorithm for surface and [solid voxelization](#1695-solid-voxelization.md) [G]. It distinguishes itself by using bit-packed storage formats and [conservative rasterization](#2936-conservative-rasterization.md) techniques adapted for GPU atomics, enabling real-time performance for interactive applications [G]. Choose it when real-time, high-throughput [voxelization](#12-voxelization.md) of triangle meshes is required on CUDA hardware [G].

### [GPU-based Voxel Query via Conditional Histogram Computation](10393-gpu-based-voxel-query-via-conditional-histogram-computation.md)
Uses conditional histograms for efficient voxel queries [G]. It distinguishes itself by focusing on query operations rather than direct mesh-to-voxel conversion [G]. Choose it when fast spatial queries or occupancy checks on an existing voxel grid are needed instead of generating the grid [G].

## Background
The method is based on the algorithm described by Schwarz and Seidel [CUDA Voxelizer GPU Voxelization](6757-cuda-voxelizer-gpu-voxelization.md). It was implemented as a high-performance, real-time solution leveraging CUDA parallelism [G]. [Atomic operations](#3684-atomic-operations-for-global-counters.md) are a key component, though they can introduce contention on older hardware architectures [G].
